$schema_note: Criterion-level completeness checklists. Passage-independent. Edit by hand — do not invent content beyond the worked gospel-clarity example. Placeholder criteria ship empty until Chris fills them.

criteria.rubric: A high score on this criterion implies the evaluation found a full gospel presentation (or named what was missing). Score alone is not enough — the checklist asks whether the evaluation noticed required elements of a gospel presentation when the sermon attempted one.

checklist.requirement: When the sermon presents the gospel (call to trust, hope, confidence, salvation), the evaluation checks whether the cross or atoning death of Christ is named or clearly implied.

When the sermon presents the gospel and orients on hope, confidence, or living hope, the evaluation checks whether the resurrection (or living Christ / risen Lord) is named as the ground of that hope.
checklist.example_failure: Hebrews 3 evaluation scoring gospel clarity 5/5 on a presentation that never names the resurrection while the sermon's own close appeals to confidence and boasting in hope.

checklist.requirement: When the sermon calls for a response (believe, hold fast, come, repent), the evaluation checks whether that response is concretely shaped by the gospel content already preached, not a generic exhortation detached from the good news just announced.

criteria.rubric: PLACEHOLDER — Chris fills. What a full treatment of this criterion requires, independent of any one passage.
